observations.title: Call to Action (CTA) Prominence
observations.detail: H&M uses a single, high-contrast, full-width 'ADD TO BAG' button anchored to the bottom, making the primary task very prominent. Zara splits the bottom area between an 'ADD' button and an 'Apple Pay' quick-action button, which distributes the visual weight.

observations.title: Product Information Density
observations.detail: Zara displays immediate textual information such as price, product name, and a brief description below the product image. H&M focuses heavily on the visual aspect of the product, with text-based details less visible in this view.

observations.title: Header Utility
observations.detail: H&M's header contains more visible utility icons (search, profile, favorites, bag) compared to Zara's more minimalist approach with only three icons.

observations.title: Visual Hierarchy
observations.detail: H&M's layout creates a strong vertical flow from the product image directly to the large action button. Zara provides a more information-dense layout that requires scanning text before reaching the action buttons.
